findings.title: D-tb-18 says the edit ledger refused the six in-kind removals, but no such pair was ever written

walk_entry.title: Members of the named provenance kinds stay in three tightened bodies, though the requirement says those kinds are removed

findings.recommendation: D-tb-18 (explore.md:304-305) says each removal 'would take characters no pattern covers, so the edit ledger refused it'. No pair for these sites was written; the ledger's coverage check would refuse one, which is why none was attempted. Reword to 'so the edit ledger's coverage check would refuse it' (or 'so none was written as a pair'), so the record states what happened.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-17T20-16-13Z.json, row 4: 'decided' gives the walk description's target as about 300, where its cited D-tb-9 says about 360
findings.recommendation: The reader takes 300 as the target, tighter than D-tb-9's 360 (and the later ledger's 400). Write a replacement whose 'decided' gives D-tb-9's figure, or says why it differs.

findings.title: ledger-2026-11-17T20-16-13Z.json, row 3: 'a strict reader of the file format', the unexplained drift-scan sentence and 'review-walk skill' slow the reader
findings.recommendation: Say 'valid YAML' as RG2 does instead of 'a strict reader of the file format' and 'the reader Claude Code uses'; say why the drift-scan description might have changed before saying it stays; name the address-reviews skill as the other ledger does. A replacement record carries the rewording.

findings.title: stop-2026-11-17T19-56-53Z.json, row 3: 'about' gives '700 characters shorter' without saying it is per body, beside the doc's 9,400 total
findings.recommendation: A reader takes 700 as the total saving and cannot square it with RG1's 9,400. Write a replacement whose 'about' says 'about 700 characters shorter in each body, as the brief estimated'.

findings.title: stop-2026-11-17T19-56-53Z.json, row 1: 'question' uses 'the stop-condition explanations' and 'the list of ledger areas', neither defined
findings.recommendation: Add both terms to the replacement's 'defines' (what the bullet's glosses of each stop condition and its eighteen named areas are), or reword the option in the doc's words.

findings.title: stop-2026-11-17T20-08-45Z.json, row 4: 'defines' gives R-crc-14's mirror corollary without its 'the copy adds nothing' condition, and says the note names the spec rather than the requirement
findings.recommendation: The definition lists three conditions; R-rop-14 shows the corollary also requires that the copy adds nothing, and that the note names the requirement. A reader takes the corollary as narrower than it is, and meets 'still adds nothing' in the resolution unexplained. Write a replacement whose definition carries all four conditions in R-rop-14's words.

findings.title: stop-2026-11-17T20-08-45Z.json, row 3: 'about' counts 'about 1,860 characters in nine places' where the resolution and R-rop-14 count thirteen notes
findings.recommendation: A reader cannot tell whether 'nine places' counts bodies or notes. The replacement says what nine counts (the notes measured at the time) beside the thirteen the stage removed.

findings.title: resolution-2026-11-17T20-16-12Z.json, row 4: 'effect' says thirteen mirror notes without squaring it with the stop's nine places
findings.recommendation: The resolution corrects the stop's 'eight specs' but then says 'thirteen mirror notes' with no word on the stop's 'nine places', so a reader thinks the scope grew between question and answer. A replacement's 'effect' adds one clause saying what nine and thirteen each count.
